title: Elliott Wave Oscillator
summary: The gap between a 5 bar and a 35 bar simple average, as a percentage of price, drawn as a green and red histogram around zero.
description:
The Elliott Wave Oscillator measures momentum as the distance between a fast and a slow simple moving average of the source: by default 5 bars and 35 bars of the close. With `Show Dif as percent of current Candle` on, the gap is divided by the source and shown as a percentage, so readings compare across instruments and price levels; with it off, the gap is shown in price.

The result is drawn as a histogram in its own pane: green while the fast average is above the slow one and red while it is at or below it.
howToRead:
Bars above zero mean the recent average is above the longer one, an upswing; bars below zero a downswing. The height shows how strong the move is, so a new high in price on a lower histogram peak is a sign the swing is tiring, and traders who count waves use the tallest peak in a run to mark the strongest leg.

The colour changes on the zero crossing, which lags the turn in price by a few bars, and in a sideways market the histogram hovers around zero and flips often.

settings.label: Source
settings.description: The price series both averages are taken over. Close is the default.

settings.label: Fast Length
settings.description: Bars in the fast simple average. 5 is the usual value.

settings.label: Slow Length
settings.description: Bars in the slow simple average. 35 is the usual value.

settings.label: Show Dif as percent of current Candle
settings.description: Show the gap as a percentage of the source instead of in price, so readings compare across instruments.

faq.q: Why use a percentage rather than price?
faq.a: A gap of 100 means a lot on one instrument and very little on another. As a percentage of price the readings mean the same on any instrument and at any price level.
When the gap crosses zero: green while the fast average is above the slow one, red while it is at or below it.

faq.q: Do I need to count waves to use it?
faq.a: No. It works as a plain momentum oscillator; the wave reading is one way to use it, not a requirement.
